facts.fact: Livebearers give birth to live young: fertilization is internal and the fry develop inside the mother, unlike egg-laying fish.
The four most common aquarium livebearers are mollies (Poecilia latipinna), guppies (Poecilia reticulata), platies (Xiphophorus maculatus) and swordtails (Xiphophorus hellerii).
Nearly all aquarium livebearers belong to the family Poeciliidae; Endler's livebearer (Poecilia wingei) and the swordtails (Xiphophorus) are among them.
Most Poeciliidae are ovoviviparous: the mother keeps the eggs in her body for protection but gives them no nutrients.
A few livebearers, such as splitfins and halfbeaks, are viviparous: embryos are fed from the mother's blood through placenta-like structures.
Livebearers are considered beginner-friendly because they are peaceful, colourful and hardy.
Gestation: guppies (Poecilia reticulata) 20-30 days, swordtails (Xiphophorus hellerii) about 30 days, platies (Xiphophorus maculatus) 25-35 days, mollies (Poecilia latipinna) up to 60 days.
Some livebearers can have broods every four to eight weeks, depending on water conditions, temperature and diet.
Females can give birth about once a month.
Male guppies (Poecilia reticulata) have a gonopodium, a stick-shaped anal fin; females have a fan-shaped anal fin.
Male mollies (Poecilia) and platies (Xiphophorus) have a pointed anal fin, females a rounded or fan-shaped one; male swordtails (Xiphophorus hellerii) have an elongated lower tail fin.
A pregnant female shows an enlarged abdomen and a dark spot near the anal fin that darkens as delivery nears.

Cá bảy màu (Poecilia reticulata) close to giving birth: the belly turns from round to square, the gravid spot grows darker and larger, the fish swims slowly with tail lowered, hides, and almost stops eating.
Cá bảy màu (Poecilia reticulata): under white light, small black dots inside the belly (the fry's eyes) mean birth is about 12–36 hours away.
Cá bảy màu (Poecilia reticulata): from the belly becoming clearly square to birth usually takes about 12–72 hours.
Cá bảy màu (Poecilia reticulata): standard pregnancy is 28–35 days at 26–28°C; a first brood may take 33–38 days, later broods (2nd–3rd on) usually 26–32 days.
Cá bảy màu (Poecilia reticulata): pregnancy lasts 20–30 days; a young female may have 8–10 fry in her first brood, later broods 25–50, mature females 40–100.
cá kiếm (Xiphophorus): pregnancy typically lasts 28 to 42 days, depending on water temperature, diet and the mother's age and health; each birth gives 10 to 100 fry.
Most livebearers do best at 74–78°F and pH 7.0–8.4; use a heater if the room is below 74°F.
Aqueon suggests 1 teaspoon of sea salt or non-iodized aquarium salt per gallon for livebearers, after confirming the other fish tolerate salt.
LiveAquaria gives livebearer water as 64–82°F, pH 5.5–8.0, KH 10–30, with a minimum tank of 20–30 gallons.
Move the pregnant female before birth into a separate 5–20 gallon breeding tank with a foam filter, a heater and floating artificial plants, without substrate.
Feed fry small amounts several times a day: baby brine shrimp (Artemia), baby fish food, or flake food ground into powder.
Move fry to the main tank after about 4–6 weeks, once they are larger than the adults' mouths.
Cá bảy màu (Poecilia reticulata): the mother can be returned to the community tank about 12–24 hours after giving birth.

Cá bảy màu (Poecilia reticulata): from day 2 after birth feed the mother light, small foods such as baby brine shrimp (Artemia) in 2–3 small meals a day; protein can be increased again after about 3–5 days.
cá kiếm (Xiphophorus): keep the breeding tank at about 26-28°C and the fry tank at 27-29°C; the mother must be removed from the breeding tank after birth.
An isolation breeder holds up to two pregnant females; slits let newborns escape into a separate section. A net or drop-in breeder is cheaper but fry outgrow it quickly.
Keep 2–3 females per male, since males constantly pursue females and can be aggressive to each other.
A single pregnant fish can quickly overwhelm an aquarium and several generations can build up within a few months; separating males and females prevents unwanted broods.
Fit a sponge pre-filter over the filter intake so fry are not sucked in.
Fry born in the main tank need dense floating cuttings to hide in, since some adults eagerly eat newborn fry.
Keep a secure lid: livebearers may jump when frightened.
Reckless inbreeding, as with 'designer' guppies (Poecilia reticulata), is a concern.
Cá bảy màu (Poecilia reticulata): separating the mother a few hours too late can let her eat all the newborn fry.
Cá bảy màu (Poecilia reticulata): mating the mother again right after birth stresses her and can give weak, poorly coloured fry; heavy feeding right after birth can cause indigestion.
Cá bảy màu (Poecilia reticulata): do not put the newly delivered mother straight back into the old tank.
Cá bảy màu (Poecilia reticulata): tap water must have its chlorine removed first, by sunning or aerating it.
cá kiếm (Xiphophorus): common mistakes are not removing the mother after birth, over- or underfeeding fry, skipping water changes, too many fry in a small tank, and ignoring lighting.
Overfeeding: give livebearers only what they eat in under 2 minutes.
Name for the term: "Livebearer"
Name for the term: "cá đẻ con"
Name for the term: "cá thai sinh"
Livebearers are omnivores needing both plant matter and meat-based foods.
